params.body:
## Why

A third of the trends on the radar named China. That reflects how much we read on the Chinese hot-search lists, not what a reader comes to Gentells for. The pipeline now marks a trend whose evidence comes mostly from East Asia with a lane (Trendwolves/gentells-pipeline#451). The site keeps those trends apart.

## What changes

- **`trend_cards.lane`** (migration): null means the main list. The reconcile stores each trend's `lane`, and the payload's `lanes` (id, label, line) go in ProjectionState.
- **`TrendCard::scopeMainList` and `TrendCard::lanes()`**.
- **Trends page**: the main list leaves lane trends out. Each lane follows below it in a band with the pipeline's label and line, filtered like the list above. It shows three cards, then "Show all N".
- **Home page and reading room**: only the main list, so a lane trend takes no place on the front.
- **A lane the site has no label for** stays in the main list instead of disappearing.

## Tests

`tests/Feature/TrendLaneTest.php` (4 tests):
- the reconcile keeps each lane and the labels;
- the band sits under the main list, even for a lane trend that ranks first;
- a lane trend is not on the front;
- an unlabelled lane stays in the main list.

In the full suite, only BuildStampTest and SocialLoginTest fail. Both are local environment issues: BuildStampTest always fails in a worktree, and SocialLoginTest because Socialite is missing from the copied vendor folder.

Merge after the pipeline PR. Until the pipeline sends `lane`, every card has none and the site looks as it does today.
params.title: Trends in a lane get their own band on the trends page, and stay off the front
